BHAKTI MOVEMENTS

Main Features of Bhakti Movement

  1. 1. The Bhakti saints opposed complicated rituals, sacrifices, and strict rules followed by traditional priests.
  2. 2. They promoted Monotheism → Worship of single God.
  3. 3. Saguna Hindu sects worshipped God in a specific form and Nirguna sects believed God has no form.

The Saguna sects were divided into two major branches:

  1. 1. Vaishnavism: They worshipped Lord Vishnu or his incarnations and were called Alvars (First female Alvar was Andal, she was a propounder of Bhakti Movement). There were 12 Alvars of Vaishnavism.
  2. 2. Shaivism: They worshipped Lord Shiva and were called Nayanars. Nayanars were a group of 63 Tamil Saints out of which 3 were females: Karaikkal Ammaiyar, Mangayarkkarasiyar and Isaignaniyar.

→ Kapalikas, Kalamukhas and Nathas are sects of Shaivism while Sahajiyas is a sect of Vaishnavism.

  • Lord Vishnu has 10 avatars → Matsya, Kurma, Varaha, Narasimha, Vamana, Parashurama, Rama, Krishna, Buddha, and Kalki.
  • Chariot: Garuda (National emblem of Indonesia)

Philosophy and Founder

PhilosophyFounder
VishishtadvaitaRamanuj Acharya
Dvaitadvaita / BhedabhedNimbark Acharya
DvaitaMadhva Acharya
ShuddhadvaitaVallabhachariya
AdvaitaSri Adi Shankaracharya
  • Shuddhadvaita teaches that the world is real and emphasizes worship through idols.
  • Sri Shankaracharya believed this life and world is a myth and did not support idol worship.

Bhakti Movement Saints

#### Kabir (1440-1510)

  • He was born in Varanasi.
  • He was a disciple of Ramananda.
  • Kabir's Doha often criticises Hindu or Islamic Dharma pointing out the contradictions and superficialities in both religions.
  • He belonged to Nirguna sect.
  • Bijaka is a compilation of the preachings by Kabir.

#### Ramananda (14th-15th Century)

  • He belonged to Nirguna sect from North India.
  • Kabir Das was his disciple.

#### Guru Nanak (1469-1538)

  • He belonged to Nirguna sect and Khatri community.

#### Vallabhacharya (1479-1531)

  • He gave Shuddhadvaita philosophy.
  • He gave the philosophy of "Pushti Marg".
  • He said "Ram and Krishna are avatars of Vishnu".

#### Vidyapati (14-15 century)

  • He composed Padavali (love ballads of Krishna and Radha).

#### Chaitanya (1486-1533)

  • He propounded Bhakti Movement in Bengal (known as Bengal Vaishnavism).
  • He is known as "King of Gaudiya". He founded Gaudiya Vaishnavism.

#### Purandar Das (1480-1564)

  • He is known as "Father of Carnatic music" (South Indian music).

#### Mirabai (1498-1546)

  • Disciple of: Raidas/Ravidas
  • She was daughter-in-law of Rana Sanga of Mewar.
  • She was a Rathore princess.
  • She was a bhakt of Krishna.

#### Surdas (1483-1563)

  • He was blind.
  • He belonged to Agra.
  • He dedicated his lifetime in bhakti of Krishna.

#### Tulsi Das (1532-1623)

  • He was a bhakt of Ram.
  • Famous writings: Ramcharitmanas, Kavita wali, Gitawali

#### Dadu Dayal (1544-1603)

  • He belonged to Nirguna sect.
  • He is the founder of Dadu Panth.

#### Sankaradeva (1449-1568)

  • He spread Bhakti Movement across Assam.
  • He is the propounder of the Sattriya dance.
  • He gave Borgeet.

#### Thyagaraja (1767-1847)

  • He was from Tamil Nadu.
  • He was a bhakt of Rama.

Bhakti Saints of Maharashtra

#### Jnanesvara / Jnanadeva (1271-1296)

  • He was the founder of Bhakti Movement in Maharashtra.
  • He wrote commentary on Bhagvad Geeta (Bhavarthadipika).
  • He composed Abhangas.

#### Namadeva (1270-1350)

  • He was the founder of Varkari sect.
  • The followers Varkari sect worshipped Vitthal (a form of Lord Vishnu worshipped in Maharashtra).

#### Ramdas (1608-1681)

  • He wrote Dasabodha (compilation of his sermons).

Bhakti Saints of Karnataka

#### Basavana

  • He founded Lingayat/Virashaiva sect.
  • He initially was a Jaina and a minister in the court of a Chalukya king in the 12th Century.
  • He was a believer of Lord Shiva (he believed in Monotheism).
  • He was against caste system / Vedic rituals.

SIKH GURUS

Era of Sikhism

Sikhs believed in three things that could abolish Untouchability. They were:

  • Langar: Community kitchen
  • Pangat: Eating
  • Sangat: Decision making

Guru Nanak Dev (1469-1539)

  • Birth: 1469, Nankana Sahib (present day: Pakistan)
  • He founded the Sikh faith.
  • Death: Kartarpur (Pakistan)
  • He started the institution of "Guru Ka Langar".
  • He was contemporary to Mughal emperor Babur.

Guru Angad Dev (1539-1552)

  • He created and introduced the Gurmukhi (written form of Punjabi) script.
  • He compiled the writings of Nanak Dev in Guru Granth Sahib in Gurmukhi Script.
  • He started Mall Akhara (wrestling arena) system.

Guru Amardas Sahib (1552-1574)

  • He introduced the Anand Karaj marriage ceremony for the Sikhs.
  • He established Manji and Piri system of religious missions for men and women respectively.
  • He was contemporary to Mughal emperor Akbar.

Guru Ram Das (1574-1581)

  • He founded the city of Amritsar (the holy city of the Sikhs).

Guru Arjan Dev (1581-1606)

  • He compiled the Adi Granth → the scriptures of the Sikhs.
  • He started the construction of the famous "Golden Temple" at Amritsar.
  • He requested the Muslim Sufi → Mian Mir to lay the cornerstone of the Harmandir Sahib.
  • He completed construction of Sri Darbar Sahib (Golden Temple). Jahangir ordered his execution, because he gave shelter to Khusrau (rebellious son of Jahangir), thus he was hailed as Shaheedan-de-Sartaj (the crown of martyrs).
  • Gold plating of this temple was done by Maharaja Ranjit Singh.

Guru Har Gobind Sahib (1606-1644)

  • Son of: Guru Arjan Dev and he was also known as a "Soldier Saint".
  • He is the first Sikh Guru to take up arms to defend the faith.
  • He waged wars against Mughal rulers Jahangir and Shah Jahan.
  • He established Akal Takht.

Guru Har Rai Sahib (1644-1661)

  • He gave shelter to Dara Shikoh, the eldest son of Mughal Ruler Shah Jahan.
  • He avoided conflict with Emperor Aurangzeb and devoted his efforts to missionary work.

Guru Har Krishan Sahib (1661-1664)

  • Guru Har Krishan was the youngest of the Gurus (became the leader at the age of 5 years).
  • He was contemporary of Aurangzeb and was summoned to Delhi by him under framed charges of Anti-Islamic blasphemy.
  • Death due to: Smallpox

Guru Tegh Bahadur Sahib (1665-1675)

  • He established the town of Anandpur.
  • He was killed by Aurangzeb in 1675 because he resisted the forceful conversion of Hindu Kashmiri Pandits.

Guru Gobind Singh Sahib (1675-1708)

  • He established Khalsa Panth in 13 April 1699 (on Vaisakhi), changing the Sikhs into a saint-soldier order to protect themselves.
  • He was the last of Sikh Gurus in human form and he passed the Guruship of the Sikhs to the Guru Granth Sahib.
  • He was assassinated by two Afghans, sent by Wazir Khan (Mughal ruler of Sirhind).
  • He was succeeded by Banda Bahadur (not a Sikh Guru), who was killed by Farrukhsiyar.

Guru Granth Sahib

  • Guru Granth Sahib (also known as the Adi Granth) is the scripture of the Sikhs.
  • The Granth was written in Gurmukhi script and it contains the actual words and verses as uttered by the Sikh Gurus.
  • It is considered the supreme spiritual authority and head of the Sikh religion, rather than any living person.

SUFI MOVEMENTS

Origin of Sufi Movements

  • In early Islamic teachings, some believed that a Dar al-Harb (Land of War) could become a Dar al-Islam (Land of Islam) through Jihad, which means striving or struggle. They also believe that Mujahid (one who engages in jihad) attains Jannat on jihad.
  • This set of belief was changed by Sufi saints.

Khwaja Ali Hujwiri (11th Century)

  • He is also known as "Data Ganj Baksh".

Shaikh Bahauddin Zakaria (1182-1262)

  • He founded the leading Khanqah in India at Multan.
  • He was the founder of the Suhrawardi (Suhrawardiyya) order.
The Naqshbandi Silsila is a chain of succession in the Naqshbandi Sufi order of Sunni Islam.

Khwaja Moinuddin Chisti (1141-1236)

  • He was the founder of the Chisti order.

Other Saints of Chisti Order

  • Sheikh Hamiduddin Nagauri (1192-1274)
  • Khwaja Qutubuddin Bakhtiar Kaki (1173–1235) — Disciple and spiritual successor of Moinuddin Chishti at the head of the Chishti order. Qutb-ud-din Aibak (a political patron, not his disciple) began construction of the Qutub Minar in his honour (foundation laid c. 1199).
  • Baba Fariduddin Masud Ganj-i-Shakar (c. 1188–1266) → He is popularly known as Baba Farid. Disciple of Qutb-ud-Din Bakhtiar Kaki and spiritual predecessor of Nizamuddin Auliya.
  • Shaikh Nizamuddin Auliya (1236-1325) → He is popularly known as Mehboob-i-Illahi.
  • Syed Muhammad Gesu Daraz → Popularly known as Bandanawaz.
  • Shaikh Nasiruddin Mahmud → He was later known as Chirag-i-Delhi.
  • Shaikh Badruddin Samarkandi (13th Century) → He founded Firdausi Order.
Ajmer Sharif built in honour of Khwaja Moinuddin Chisti. Mohammad Bin Tuglaq was the first Sultan to visit Ajmer Sharif.
